projects.name: Breathapplyser
projects.description: Modern breathalyzer app with advanced tracking, caffeine monitoring, social features, and comprehensive analytics (2026). Includes legacy version (2024).

caseStudy.claim: Mobile breathalyzer companion (2026 redesign) with BAC and caffeine tracking, graphs, social features, and PDF reports.
caseStudy.role: TODO(verify): Product engineer / full-stack for app and web surfaces
caseStudy.problem:
Drink tracking apps are often either too simplistic or too clinical to use in social settings.

Breathapplyser needed clear BAC/caffeine graphs, fast logging, and optional social accountability.

sections.title: Home
sections.body:
Modern home screen for current levels and quick actions.

Entry point for drinks, graphs, and history.

sections.title: BAC over time
sections.body:
Interactive BAC graph so users see how levels change over time.

Paired with drink history for context.

sections.title: Drink presets
sections.body: Presets speed up logging common drinks without re-entering details every time.

sections.title: PDF report generation
sections.body: PDF reports for personal tracking and health insights from logged history.

decisions.why: Users often manage both stimulants and depressants in the same night.
decisions.tradeoff: Richer data model and more graph surfaces to maintain.

decisions.choice: Full V2 redesign rather than incremental UI polish
decisions.why: Legacy UX could not carry social features and reporting cleanly.
decisions.tradeoff: Temporary dual narrative (legacy vs modern) on the case study.

decisions.why: Reach users on both installable and browser entry points.
decisions.tradeoff: Two distribution channels to keep aligned.

caseStudy.outcome: Shipped V2 with BAC/caffeine graphs, presets, friend codes/leaderboards, and PDF reports, plus web and download.breathapplyser.online surfaces.

projects.description: Enterprise financial education platform (SpZero) built for SPZeroFinance with interactive learning modules, video content, quizzes, calculator widgets, and comprehensive analytics

caseStudy.claim: Suite of financial literacy tools — education modules, calculators, quizzes, and budgeting — under one LifeSmart hub.
caseStudy.role: TODO(verify): Full-stack engineer across multiple LifeSmart products
caseStudy.problem:
Financial literacy content is scattered, and calculators rarely connect to a coherent learning journey.

LifeSmart needed modular tools that still feel like one brand.

sections.title: SpZero learning platform
sections.body:
Module-based financial education with video/slide content, quizzes, and progress saving.

Admin analytics track engagement across modules and users.

sections.title: Interactive learning path
sections.body:
Visual module progression across foundations, personal finance, credit, and investing.

Keeps learners oriented without a flat content dump.

sections.title: Budget tool flow
sections.body:
LifeBalance-style budgeting steps that walk users through income and spending decisions.

Designed as a guided multi-step tool rather than a blank spreadsheet.

sections.title: Asset simulation results
sections.body:
Asset market simulation with results visualisation for teaching investment concepts.

Charts make outcomes tangible after learners run a scenario.

decisions.choice: Product suite with shared hub, separate tool deploys
decisions.why: Different tools have different stacks and release cadences.
decisions.tradeoff: More surfaces to keep branded and linked from the hub.

decisions.choice: Cloudflare Workers + Postgres for SpZero-class apps
decisions.why: Edge performance with durable relational data for progress and admin.
decisions.tradeoff: More moving parts than a single Firebase app.

decisions.why: Learners should not create yet another account for partner content.

caseStudy.outcome: Delivered a hub plus specialized tools (education, calculators, quiz, budget, simulation, buzzer) used in production financial-literacy contexts.

projects.name: Bgr8
projects.description: Comprehensive mentoring and community platform with intelligent mentor-mentee matching

caseStudy.claim: Mentoring platform with a proprietary MentorAlgorithm scoring across 70+ criteria for mentor–mentee pairing.
caseStudy.problem:
Matching mentors and mentees by hand does not scale, and shallow filters miss compatibility.

Bgr8 needed a weighted scoring system, real-time booking, and admin tools that operators could trust.

sections.title: Weighted matching algorithm
sections.body:
The MentorAlgorithm applies weighted scoring across skills, experience, availability, location, and compatibility factors.

Built in TypeScript with real-time data processing so recommendations stay current as profiles change.

sections.title: Mentee dashboard
sections.body:
Personalized dashboard with mentor recommendations and progress tracking.

Firebase Firestore keeps recommendations and status in sync without full page reloads.

sections.title: Live messaging
sections.body:
Real-time messaging between mentors and mentees with delivery and presence cues.

Firebase-backed so conversations stay available across sessions.
sections.imageAlt: Live messaging between mentor and mentee

sections.title: Admin analytics
sections.body:
Admin analytics for engagement, matching outcomes, and platform growth.

Operators get live Firestore listeners and exportable reporting.

decisions.choice: Custom MentorAlgorithm instead of simple tag filters
decisions.why: Mentoring quality depends on many soft signals that OR-filters cannot express.
decisions.tradeoff: Higher implementation and tuning cost versus a simpler search UI.

decisions.choice: Firebase for realtime data and auth
decisions.why: Needed live dashboards, messaging, and rapid iteration without running a custom socket fleet.
decisions.tradeoff: Vendor coupling and careful rules for admin query surfaces.

decisions.why: Avoid rebuilding calendar conflict resolution and booking UX.
decisions.tradeoff: External dependency for a core user journey.

caseStudy.outcome: Shipped a production mentoring platform with matching, Cal.com booking, RBAC admin tools, and multi-layered security (CSP, XSS protections, rate limiting).

projects.name: Therabot
projects.description: Whatsapp & Webchat Chatbot designed to provide conversational support therapy.

caseStudy.claim: Mental health support chatbot on web and WhatsApp, with guided sessions, tone controls, and conversation history.
caseStudy.problem:
People need low-friction mental health support outside clinic hours, without a heavy app install.

Therabot had to feel safe, configurable, and available on channels people already use.

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.body:
Central dashboard for session status and quick access into chat.

Designed for calm, readable scanning rather than dense admin chrome.

sections.title: Role and tone settings
sections.body:
Operators can tune role and tone so responses stay appropriate for the support context.

Settings screens keep those controls explicit instead of buried prompts.

sections.title: Active web chat
sections.body:
Web chat for anonymous or signed-in sessions with conversation continuity.

History views let users revisit earlier guidance.

sections.title: WhatsApp surface
sections.body:
WhatsApp integration meets users in a familiar messenger.

Same support model, different entry point.

decisions.why: Needed flexible natural-language support rather than a rigid decision tree alone.
decisions.tradeoff: Must constrain tone/role carefully for a mental-health context.

decisions.why: Reach users where they already communicate.
decisions.tradeoff: Two clients to keep behaviour consistent.

decisions.why: Fast path to auth, persistence, and a deployable Node/React app.
decisions.tradeoff: Operational split across services to monitor.

caseStudy.outcome: Shipped guided meditations, personalized tips, anonymous chat, conversation history, and a WhatsApp channel alongside the web app.
